title: B2+ · L16 — Phrasal verbs (C1 abstract)
description: Phrasal verbs abstractos de nivel C1: bring about, come across, follow up on, boil down to, y otros.

questions.prompt: Lees en un informe corporativo: 'The new policy brought about significant changes in workplace culture.'
questions.question: 'The new policy brought about significant changes' means:
questions.explanation: 'Bring about' = causar, provocar, producir (siempre resultado). Uso frecuente en escritos formales, academicos y business — mas pulido que 'cause' o 'make happen'. Registro elevado: aparece en editoriales, papers, y speeches ejecutivos. Sinonimos: cause, generate, produce, effect (verbo), give rise to. OJO al orden: usualmente inseparable ('brought about + noun'), aunque con pronombres se separa ('brought them about'). Error hispano: interpretar literal 'traer sobre' — nada que ver con movimiento fisico.
examples: The reform brought about a fundamental shift in workplace culture over five years.
His leadership brought about record-breaking growth in two consecutive quarters. → business context

questions.prompt: Tu profesor te dice: 'I came across an interesting article on your topic yesterday.'
questions.question: 'I came across an interesting article' means:
questions.explanation: 'Come across' tiene DOS significados C1 esenciales: (1) encontrar por casualidad (uso mas comun); (2) parecer/dar impresion sobre uno mismo — 'she comes across as arrogant' = 'da la impresion de ser arrogante'. Ambos usos son extremadamente frecuentes en spoken y written. Registro: neutro (funciona en casual y professional). Error hispano tipico: pensar en movimiento fisico. Colocacion nativa: 'come across as + adjective' (dar imagen de), 'come across a book/article/person' (encontrar).
examples: I came across your paper while doing research for my thesis last week. → uso 1 (encontrar)
He came across as nervous during the interview, though he actually knew his stuff. → uso 2 (parecer)

questions.statement: 'It boils down to trust' means the issue essentially reduces to a matter of trust.
questions.explanation: VERDADERO. 'Boil down to' = reducirse a lo esencial cuando eliminas complejidad. Metafora culinaria potente: como cocinar una salsa hasta el concentrado — te queda la esencia. Uso frecuente en business, filosofia, y analisis. Nunca fisico literal (aunque literal 'boil down' existe en cocina). Formulas nativas: 'it all boils down to X', 'ultimately, this boils down to Y'. Registro: neutro-elevado, funciona en boardroom y en podcast. Colocacion: siempre + 'to' + sustantivo o gerundio.
examples: Ultimately, the decision boils down to values — not spreadsheets. → contraste dramatico
It all boils down to whether we prioritize speed or quality. → binary framing

questions.prompt: Al final de una reunion tu CEO dice: 'Great discussion — let's follow up on that idea next week.'
questions.question: 'Let's follow up on that idea next week' means:
options: Take further action based on it.
questions.explanation: 'Follow up on' = dar seguimiento, tomar accion posterior sobre algo. Ubicuo en business English — probablemente el phrasal verb #1 en meetings corporativos. Dual uso: verbo ('follow up on X') y sustantivo ('a follow-up meeting', 'send a follow-up'). Diferencia sutil con 'follow through' — follow up = continuar la conversacion; follow through = ejecutar hasta el final lo prometido. Registro: business universal. Error hispano: confundir con 'follow' simple (seguir fisicamente).
examples: I'll follow up on that lead by Thursday and let you know what I find. → uso verbo
Great meeting — I'll send a follow-up email with action items shortly. → uso sustantivo

questions.text: The proposal was carried out despite significant pushback from senior stakeholders.
questions.explanation: Frase corporativa densa con dos phrasal verbs C1. Fenomeno de connected speech: 'carried out' con catenacion /ˈkæridaʊt/ (t-flap US); 'pushback' se dice como una unidad /ˈpʊʃbæk/; 'senior stakeholders' con weak /ˈsiːnjəˈsteɪkhəʊldəz/. Vocabulario clave: 'carry out' = ejecutar, implementar (mas pulido que 'do' o 'complete'); 'pushback' = resistencia, oposicion (sustantivo del phrasal verb 'push back' = disentir). Colocaciones: 'significant pushback', 'senior stakeholders'. Registro: business meeting o report.
examples: The plan was carried out with remarkable efficiency despite the complexity involved.
Despite pushback from finance, we carried out the pilot as originally planned.

questions.prompt: Discutes los ultimos detalles de un contrato: 'We need to iron out the details before signing.'
questions.question: 'We need to iron out the details before signing' means:
questions.explanation: 'Iron out' = resolver, alisar detalles pendientes o problemas remanentes. Metafora domestica potente: como planchar arrugas fuera de una camisa — eliminar imperfecciones que quedan. Muy comun en contratos, negociaciones, planes de proyecto. Colocaciones nativas: 'iron out kinks', 'iron out wrinkles', 'iron out details', 'iron out differences'. Registro: neutro-professional. Error hispano: interpretar literal como planchar ropa. Formula: 'iron out' + noun (los issues/details/kinks).
examples: We need to iron out the last few issues in the contract before Friday.
Let's meet Friday to iron out the timeline and lock in the dates. → 'lock in' otra colocacion

questions.prompt: Empareja cada phrasal verb comunicativo C1 con su traduccion:
questions.explanation: Seis phrasal verbs esenciales del discurso analitico C1. Aparecen constantemente en meetings, presentaciones y debates — sin ellos, tu ingles suena limitado y traducido. 'Bring up' vs 'point out': bring up introduce tema nuevo; point out senala algo ya presente. 'Come up with' vs 'put forward': come up with es idear creativamente; put forward es proponer formalmente. 'Back up' = respaldar con evidencia (no confundir con 'back up files' — copiar). Todos separables con pronombres ('bring it up', 'back her up').
examples: She came up with a brilliant solution that no one else had considered.
Let me sum up the main points before we move on to the next agenda item.

questions.target: The evidence backs up the theory, but I'd like to point out one caveat before we jump to conclusions.
questions.explanation: Combina TRES phrasal verbs C1 en una frase natural: 'back up' (respaldar), 'point out' (senalar), 'jump to conclusions' (sacar conclusiones apresuradas). 'Caveat' /ˈkæviæt/ es sustantivo latino formal para 'advertencia/salvedad'. Discurso analitico nativo tipico de meetings intelectualmente exigentes. Ritmo natural: tono reflexivo, pausas marcadas tras 'theory,' y 'caveat', enfasis en 'one caveat'. Contracciones: 'I'd' obligatoria — 'I would' rompe fluidez. Registro: business/academic conversation nivel senior.
examples: The data back up the hypothesis, though I'd point out a limitation in the methodology.
I want to bring up something important before we sum up the discussion. → tres verbos

questions.prompt: En una entrevista te dicen: 'What makes you stand out from the other candidates?'
questions.question: 'She stands out from the other candidates' means:
questions.explanation: 'Stand out' = destacar, sobresalir positivamente. Muy usado en interviews, applications, marketing, product reviews. 'What makes you stand out?' es LA pregunta clasica de entrevista behavioural — preparate con ejemplo especifico. Colocaciones: 'stand out from the crowd' (destacar entre la multitud — muy nativo), 'stand out for X quality'. Registro: neutro-positive. Error hispano: interpretar literal como estar de pie afuera. Existe forma sustantivo 'a standout' = un ejemplo destacado.
examples: Her presentation stood out for its clarity and depth of analysis. → 'stand out for X'
The product stands out in a crowded market thanks to its user experience. → 'crowded market' colocacion

questions.statement: 'To dwell on' something means to focus on it too much, often negatively.
questions.explanation: VERDADERO. 'Dwell on' = extenderse/insistir sobre algo, con connotacion USUALMENTE negativa (ruminacion no productiva). 'Don't dwell on your mistakes' = no te obsesiones con tus errores. Muy usado en consejos, feedback, terapia, y coaching. Otra acepcion original: 'dwell' = residir/habitar (arcaico) — 'dwell on' viene metaforicamente de 'residir mentalmente en X'. Registro: neutro-elevado. Colocacion: 'dwell on the past', 'dwell on mistakes', 'no need to dwell on it'.
examples: I don't want to dwell on the past — let's focus on the fix going forward.
She tends to dwell on small mistakes, which slows down her progress. → observacion critica

questions.prompt: Te avisan que el trato con un cliente importante no salio bien: 'Unfortunately, the deal fell through at the last minute.'
questions.question: 'The plan fell through at the last minute' means:
questions.explanation: 'Fall through' = fracasar, no materializarse (planes, negocios, deals, acuerdos). Metafora fisica potente: caerse a traves de una grieta y desaparecer. Muy usado en business y personal life. NO significa postponer (seria 'push back' o 'delay') NI cancelar formalmente (seria 'call off') — sino colapsar por circunstancias. Colocaciones: 'the deal fell through', 'plans fell through', 'the sale fell through'. Registro: neutro. Error hispano: confundir con 'fall in' o 'fall down' (caidas literales).
examples: The deal fell through when the buyer withdrew financing at the last minute.
Our vacation plans fell through due to the storm — we're rebooking for spring.

questions.text: The initiative was set up to address a gap that had gone unnoticed for years.
questions.explanation: Frase abstracta corporativa/social. Fenomeno de connected speech: 'set up' con /tʌ/ /setʌp/ (t-flap en US); 'address a' con /sə/ /əˈdresə/; 'gone unnoticed' con /nʌ/ /ɡɒnʌnˈnəʊtɪst/. Vocabulario C1: 'set up' = establecer/crear (empresa, iniciativa, meeting, sistema); 'go unnoticed' = pasar desapercibido (construccion con go + past participle, muy nativa). 'Address a gap' es colocacion pulida (abordar una brecha/necesidad). Registro: business/nonprofit.
examples: The nonprofit was set up to tackle food insecurity in underserved communities.
The bug had gone unnoticed for months until the security audit flagged it.

questions.prompt: En una discusion estrategica te recuerdan: 'Let's not lose sight of the bigger picture.'
questions.question: 'Let's not lose sight of the bigger picture' means:
options: Don't forget the broader context / long-term goal.
questions.explanation: 'Lose sight of' = perder de vista (metaforico — dejar de percibir mentalmente). 'The bigger picture' = contexto amplio, meta a largo plazo, vision estrategica. Colocacion combinada muy comun en strategy, leadership, y coaching. Se opone a 'get lost in the weeds' (perderse en detalles). Formulas nativas: 'don't lose sight of X', 'keep the bigger picture in mind', 'zoom out to see the bigger picture'. Registro: business estrategico. Error hispano: interpretar literal como perdida de vista fisica.
examples: In the details, we mustn't lose sight of the strategic goal we set out to achieve.
Let's zoom out — the bigger picture matters more than these tactical questions. → 'zoom out' pareado

questions.statement: 'To weigh in on' a discussion means to add one's opinion to it.
questions.explanation: VERDADERO. 'Weigh in on' = intervenir con opinion (usualmente con peso experto o autoridad). Metafora del boxeo/pesos: 'weigh in' original = subir a la bascula antes de pelea (mostrar peso/categoria). Colocacion profesional muy usada: 'the CEO weighed in on the debate' = el CEO intervino con su vista autorizada. Formulas: 'weigh in on X', 'weigh in with an opinion'. Diferencia sutil con 'chime in' (mas casual, sin peso especial) o 'jump in' (interrumpir para intervenir). Registro: professional/analytical.
examples: The CFO weighed in on the pricing strategy and shifted the whole discussion.
I'd love to hear your perspective — please weigh in whenever you're ready. → invitacion educada

questions.target: This new direction was brought about by shifting market conditions, but it all boils down to whether we can execute quickly.
questions.explanation: Frase ejecutiva sofisticada que combina DOS phrasal verbs C1 abstractos: 'bring about' (causar — passive: 'was brought about by') + 'boil down to' (reducirse a). Muestra dominio del vocabulario abstracto anglo. 'Shifting market conditions' es colocacion economica pulida. Ritmo natural: pausa marcada tras 'conditions,' antes del pivote 'but'; enfasis en 'boils down to' y 'quickly'. Contracciones: 'it's' se contrae naturalmente si se acelera. Registro: business ejecutivo / strategic conversation nivel senior.
examples: The change was brought about by regulation, but ultimately it boils down to leadership commitment.
The pivot came about slowly, though it boils down to a single insight from customer research.
